title: YOUR WALLET HAS A FINGERPRINT
subtitle: THE CHAIN ISN'T THE ONLY PLACE YOU LEAK.

blocks.text: A SHIELDED TRANSACTION CAN HIDE PAYMENT DETAILS ON-CHAIN. IT DOES NOT MAKE THE DEVICE THAT BROADCAST IT INVISIBLE.
PRIVACY HAS MORE THAN ONE LAYER.

When people talk about cryptocurrency privacy, they usually stare at the ledger. That is only one surface. A wallet also constructs transactions, chooses fees, connects to network infrastructure and broadcasts data over the internet. Those layers can reveal information that the shielded protocol itself was never designed to hide.

Zcash documentation makes this distinction explicitly: the Zcash peer-to-peer network uses IP addresses over TCP and does not itself obfuscate a user's IP address. A network observer may therefore be able to correlate transactions or other traffic with an IP address even when the payment details are shielded.
01 // THE LEDGER AND THE NETWORK ARE DIFFERENT OBSERVATION POINTS

Orchard is designed to protect transaction information inside its shielded pool. Its cryptography can conceal details such as the addresses and transferred values of shielded actions while still allowing consensus rules to be verified. But the proof carried by the transaction and the network connection used to relay that transaction are different things.

If an observer can see traffic leaving a particular internet connection and also watch transactions propagate through the peer-to-peer network, timing and network information may create correlations. That does not mean every transaction can automatically be traced to an IP address. It means ledger privacy should not be mistaken for network-layer anonymity.
ZERO KNOWLEDGE CAN HIDE A WITNESS. IT DOES NOT HIDE YOUR IP PACKETS.
02 // METADATA CAN REBUILD CONTEXT

Zcash's privacy guidance warns users not to leak transaction IDs, transaction amounts or counterparty information because those details can create linkages. This is an important limit to understand: cryptography can remove information from the public ledger, but information disclosed somewhere else can still reconnect events.

Imagine a shielded payment followed by a public post containing the exact amount, approximate time and recipient. The shielded protocol has not failed. The user has supplied external context that an observer can compare against whatever information remains visible at the boundaries.
03 // EVEN FEES ARE A SIGNAL

Zcash documentation notes that transaction fees are publicly visible even for shielded transactions. It recommends allowing privacy-focused wallet software to select fees rather than manually choosing unusual values. A fee does not reveal the shielded recipient or amount, but distinctive public metadata can make one transaction stand out from the crowd.
This is the broader fingerprint problem. Privacy is often weakened not by one catastrophic disclosure but by several small, individually harmless-looking signals becoming useful when combined.
04 // WALLET SOFTWARE IS PART OF THE PRIVACY MODEL

A protocol specifies what the network accepts. A wallet decides how a user actually interacts with that protocol. Transaction construction, fee selection, address handling, server connections and network routing can therefore affect practical privacy. Two users of the same underlying protocol can expose different metadata because their software and behavior are different.
That is why a claim such as 'this coin is private' is incomplete. The useful question is narrower: private against which observer, at which layer, under what behavior?
05 // SHIELDING STILL CHANGES THE GRAPH

None of this makes shielded transactions pointless. Quite the opposite. Removing addresses and values from the public transaction graph eliminates powerful sources of ledger-level surveillance. But eliminating one observation surface does not automatically eliminate every other one.

Good privacy engineering is layered. Protect the ledger. Minimize metadata. Understand the network path. Be careful with what is disclosed to counterparties and public services. The cryptography can do its job perfectly while another layer gives the game away.
THE TRANSACTION CAN BE SHIELDED WHILE THE CONTEXT AROUND IT IS NOT.
